# Lesson 11 · The prototype under review

This is the prototype repository referenced by the platform modernisation
proposal for Albert's Marketplace. **Read it alongside the proposal.**

**Everything here was generated by a large language model**, from the same
prompt as the proposal document. A human checked that it is syntactically
valid and that it reads plausibly. **Nobody checked whether it is correct.**

**Every value in this repository is invented.** There are no real credentials,
project identifiers or customer records anywhere in it.

## What is here

| File | Proposal section |
|---|---|
| `ingestion/consume_clickstream.py` | §3, the clickstream consumer |
| `ingestion/connector.json` | §3, the database connector's configuration |
| `transform/models/marts/fct_order_lines.sql` | §6, the central mart |
| `transform/models/marts/schema.yml` | §6, its tests |
| `Dockerfile` | §7, how the jobs are packaged |
| `ci-build.yml` | §7, the build pipeline (lives at `.github/workflows/build.yml`) |
| `orchestration/dags/marketplace.py` | §8, the DAG |
| `infra/terraform/main.tf` | §9, the declared infrastructure |

**You do not need this repository to review the proposal.** Every point the
document makes can be judged from the document. What the files let you do is
**check whether the document is telling the truth** — which is a different
question, and often a more interesting one.

## The full file listing

The prototype contains more than the files reproduced here. This is the whole
of it, as `git ls-files` prints it:

```text
.gitignore
Dockerfile
ci-build.yml
ingestion/connector.json
ingestion/consume_clickstream.py
ingestion/requirements.txt
infra/terraform/main.tf
infra/terraform/terraform.tfstate
infra/terraform/.terraform.lock.hcl
orchestration/dags/marketplace.py
transform/dbt_project.yml
transform/models/marts/fct_order_lines.sql
transform/models/marts/schema.yml
transform/models/staging/stg_orders.sql
warehouse/daily_report.sql
```

:::note Why the listing rather than the files
Two files in that listing are not reproduced in this folder.
`terraform.tfstate` is one of them: this course publishes its lab material to a
public repository, and the automated check that guards it refuses **any** file
whose name ends in `.tfstate`, with no exceptions.

That refusal is the right behaviour, and it is also the point. Nobody discovers
a committed state file by opening it — you notice it **in the listing**, which
is exactly where you are looking now.
:::
